doc.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023

title: Leading the Harry James band: standards and Everett Longstreth
summary: How Radke sets expectations since 1989, and Everett Longstreth's advice not to yell but simply not call a player again.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: When you get a concert to do and you have to plug in a few players, is there something you say to them to get them in the spirit of the Harry James sound?

Well they know what I expect. You know I’ve been doing this since 1989, I mean running the band. And you know, you get your guys throughout the country, they know what you expect, they know what your standards are. If you’re a young guy then it’s really important to sit down and listen to the music to feel out what era you’re playing. And there’s some tough things on this book. I don’t think it’s tough, but I’ve been told by guys that “Jeez, Fred, it’s not an easy book, man.” I said, “What do you mean?” “It’s not easy.” But no, I don’t have that problem. I don’t have that problem. When I walk on stage and even my college kids I used to say, “Okay gentlemen, saddle up, lock and load and take no prisoners. You know let’s go out and do it, man.” And that’s just my attitude.
What kinds of things might happen with an individual where you would either have to let them go or not call them again?
Do you know who Everett Longstreth is?
Do you know who Everett Longstreth is?

A great arranger, great trumpet player with Woody Herman, Berklee School of Music, New England, MIT. Greg Caputo’s good friend, that’s where I met Greg. Contractor. Great trumpet player. And Everett — I owe Everett a lot. He’s re-done a lot of the arrangements and things. And he says, “You never yell at a guy, you just don’t call them anymore.” You know so and if you walked on my bandstand and you’re 15 minutes late, “Oh man I’m really sorry I’m late man, you won’t believe what — ” I don’t want to hear. If you’re late, you have an excuse, I don’t care what your excuse is, just don’t be late again. If you’re drunk on the bandstand, okay, that’s cool, once. But don’t do it again. Don’t embarrass me. And even when we were out on the road with a younger band on that Fiftieth Anniversary tour of Harry James, the band — Harry never let the band get
loose. It wasn’t like, hey man, you know. As soon as it started getting a little too relaxed he’d pull it together.
